title: Filo Cultivation Plan – Prologue
text: “Motoyasu-kun.”
“Leave it to me, I say.”
Lazy Pig’s presence bothered me, but I smashed through Éclair’s cell and destroyed the shackles binding her hands and feet, rescuing her.
“Hey. What happened after that? What are you planning to do with me?”
“I already got permission, don’t worry. Éclair-san, I want you to come with us until we can meet the queen. Shion… Liberacion will be happy too, I think.”
“What exactly did you do?”
“I knew the king and princess were going to harass me somehow. They sicced Itsuki… the Bow Hero on me and challenged me to a duel, so I made your custody the stakes and won.”
“Wha—”
Éclair was speechless. Was something strange about that?
“Of course that king tried to make excuses, but the other Heroes accepted it, so he can’t complain any further.”

“…Understood. It concerns me a little, but… later I’ll have a word with the king myself, and until I meet the queen, I’ll accompany you. Judgment can wait until after that. My name is Éclair Seaetto. I’ll be in your care for a while.”
“Yep. So… um, Shion got so mad he nearly went berserk, so we had to knock him out and now he’s sleeping it off, but I’ll leave him to you.”
“I— I see… understood, but Shion… his appearance has changed quite a bit, hasn’t it?”

Éclair looked over at the unconscious crocodile man with something like admiration, staring intently. I’d put him to sleep pretty thoroughly, after all. He’d be out cold for at least a few days, I say.
“There’s been a lot going on. I’m sure there’s plenty to catch up on, but let’s save the details for after he wakes up.”
“R-right. Ngh…”
Éclair swayed unsteadily.
“Want to ride on Kou’s back?”
Kou transformed into Filolial form right there and sat down so Éclair could climb on.
“Ah, ah… well then, I’ll take you up on that offer.”
Éclair looked startled, but climbed on obediently enough, it seemed.
“Well then, let’s head home, I say!”
And so we left the castle and headed back. Incidentally, on the way home some mysterious adventurers picked fights with us about three times, but I knocked them out without a second thought, indeed.
“Ahh, I’m exhausted. Mentally, I mean. Once we got back, we had to have a victory party on our end too.”

At the victory celebration held after our return, I too spent an enjoyable time, indeed. Since we’d brought Éclair back with us, introductions were made all over again. And so, in the tent the monster merchant had prepared, Father sat on the edge of the bed looking utterly worn out.
“Well done today, I say.”
“Yeah. Shion’s… well, we managed to bring him around with smelling salts, but Motoyasu-kun, I wish you’d held back a little.”
“I did hold back, but the effect was weak, I say. That one’s quite the promising crocodile.”
“He was furious, though… I don’t think we can let Shion near that king again.”
“Bring him along next time we show someone a taste of hell—that should clear his head, I say.”

Actually, I’d once let the Filolial Sage witness the end of Fleon-chan’s killer, so there was precedent. Incidentally, when the crocodile man woke up, Father and Éclair were both present, and once he understood the situation he seemed to calm down. Apparently his memory had blanked out right around the part where he charged at Trash and I stabbed him, because he gave quite a jolt when he came to that part. Afterward, once he learned the full circumstances, he shot me some dissatisfied looks, but I paid it no mind, I say. Still, he seemed rather pleased that he’d gained better control over his own body than before. He’d been showing off his crocodile form to Keel and Elephant. Apparently he’d grown quite massive, and there was talk of him becoming the second line of defense for everyone, right after Father.
“There was a lot going on, so I’m beat today. Wonder what tomorrow’s going to look like.”
“Father, starting tomorrow I have a request, I say.”
Indeed. I’d been holding back until now, but the Filo-tan Plan was finally set into motion.
“Oh right, you had a request, didn’t you, Motoyasu-kun? What was it again?”
“It’s about time we raised Filo-tan properly, I say. For that, I’d like you to carry out the plan that you and the others worked out in the previous loop.”
“Right, got it, but… how do we do that?”
I explained to Father the plan that he and the others had worked out in the previous loop.

“I see. So we’re recreating the process by which Filo was born… I’m a little worried whether I can pull it off properly, but since you’ve helped me out with so much, Motoyasu-kun, I suppose I’ll give it a shot.”
“Indeed, I say.”
“She’s the one you’ve fallen for, after all. Gotta do my best on this one…”

Father answered with something like a wry smile. I wondered if something was on his mind, but he wouldn’t tell me what. Later, from what Rival and the others said, apparently he felt guilty about having decided Filo-tan’s fate, even if it was for my sake. I too felt a pang of guilt about it being a choice between Filo-tan and Sakura-chan.
“So starting tomorrow my actions are pretty much decided, but what about you, Motoyasu-kun?”
“Tomorrow I’m going to go collect my reward money, I say. No sense leaving free money on the table, after all. Kuro-chan’s also been wanting to see Ren.”
“You’re actually going to collect it after all that…? Well, I did say I wasn’t going, so I can’t really stop you.”
“Of course, I say. Éclair also says she needs to go back to the castle at some point to confront Trash about the truth of things. No need to trouble you with that, Father.”

“I’m a little worried, but… there’s nobody who can actually stop you, Motoyasu-kun, and since I can’t go either, I guess it can’t be helped. The one thing to watch out for is that this whole incident is probably going to bring more attackers our way.”
“If more show up, I’ll just ship them off again, I say.”
“And that’s how the bad rumors keep spreading, huh… how am I supposed to explain this to Éclair-san…”
“If it’s too much trouble, I’ll just ship Éclair off to the queen right away, I say.”
“The way you put that… I just need to know where she ends up, that’s all.”
“In any case, Éclair seems like the type who’ll understand if you talk it through with her, I say.”

According to Father, she was serious but reasonable—someone with real integrity, so long as you gave her a proper explanation. When she’d dueled Panda, Panda had used a sneak attack, calling it fair play for a mercenary, but Éclair never once called the tactic cowardly. Capturing the Three Heroes Church fanatics who disguised themselves as bandits to raid carriages, then selling them off to Siltvelt—that wouldn’t be a problem for her either. After all, those were the ones who’d slaughtered nearly every adult in Éclair’s territory and sold the children off as slaves.
“Éclair will probably grumble at first over something this minor, but she’ll come around quickly enough, I say.”
“…Maybe I should just hand the whole explanation off to Shion. If she has complaints, I’m sure Shion would’ve already protested our outrageous behavior, and he’ll probably explain it well enough.”

Now that I thought about it, even back in the original world, Éclair had been fairly harsh toward the remnants of the Three Heroes Church. Oh, right—I recall Ren scolding her and Assistant for eagerly stripping bandits of their belongings. Regardless, this was Éclair we were talking about. She’d probably settle in surprisingly fast, I say. Flexible thinking, that’s the type she was. Come to think of it, Elephant and Éclair seemed to get along well, both being knights by station. Elephant had the better administrative skills, so much so that Éclair would come complaining to Father and Ren about her often enough—a sign of how close they’d gotten.

“It’s reassuring that you know the future, Motoyasu-kun, so we can move forward with confidence. Though we shouldn’t overdo the good deeds, apparently, so I hope things keep going smoothly like this.”
“I think it’s going well, I say.”
I felt like I was managing to act differently than before. And within that, I intended to keep taking different actions going forward.
“Vau, vau.”
Just then, Wolf found Father, came into the tent, and started nuzzling up to him.
“There, there, Wolf. You fought well today, waited patiently, enjoyed the party—you did a great job.”
“Wa-owwn! Vau vau!”
Wolf struck a flexing pose while looking in the direction of the crocodile man.
“That’s right. Shion’s gotten really reliable, hasn’t he? He told us his real name, and it seems like he’s trying to get along with everyone.”
“Vau.”
“Maybe sometime soon we could visit Éclair-san and Shion’s place.”
I think Father worries far too much about Éclair and the others, honestly.
